key_insight: The paper develops a reduced-order model showing how porous drag, wall compliance, and peristaltic motion jointly control flow and pressure in a non-axisymmetric annular conduit.
engineering_relevance: This provides a mechanistic framework for predicting cerebrospinal fluid transport in periarterial spaces where both wall deformation and porous pathways can significantly alter hydraulic resistance.
method: Adds a Darcy–Brinkman term to represent porous-medium drag in the axial momentum equation.
Couples fluid flow with compliant outer-wall displacement in a two-way fluid–structure interaction model.
Perturbs the resistance changes from peristalsis and wall motion to reduce the system to a single nonlinear pressure PDE.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a reduced-order analytical framework and notes that closed-form analytical solutions are possible for small-amplitude peristaltic waves.
watch_item: The reduced model relies on perturbative small-amplitude assumptions, so accuracy may degrade for stronger wall motion or highly nonlinear flow regimes.
paper_title: Flow in a porous non-axisymmetric annular conduit: Coupling wall compliance and peristalsis
